relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a girl with a TNFAIP3 nonsense variant: 'It revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20)'.
method_note: Hand extraction, built with a short script in scratch; all spans checked verbatim by script. Rows: the index patient (label 'patient', rule 5) and her father ('father of patient'; untested but described as affected with recurrent fever and tonsillitis). Mother and younger sister are mentioned only as untested ('her parents refused' NGS) with no individual-level facts, so they get no rows. No variant row for the father: he was not tested. Variant: cDNA 'c.547C>T'; protein printed as 'p.Arg183*' in the Fig. 1 legend and as 'p.Arg183^*' in the Discussion (conversion artefact); Fig. 1 title spells the gene 'TNFIP3', text 'TNFAIP3'. The paper's wording 'The c.547C>T mutation of the proband was detected in the patient' is ambiguous (who 'the proband' is), recorded as the patient's variant. Zygosity and inheritance not stated (no parental testing). Age at last evaluation recorded as '9-year-old' (age at presentation; follow-up continued at least 9 months after colchicine; no later age stated). Country 'Korea' taken from 'only 2 patients, including our case, have been diagnosed with HA20 in Korea'. Table 1 laboratory values: autoantibodies stated Negative recorded as excluded (D-27); ANA positive recorded observed; anti-dsDNA IgG (22.6/12.8 IU/mL), C3, C4 and blood counts at later time points have no stated interpretation and are not recorded as features; cytopenia left not reported. Checklist: 'no uveitis' does not exclude the broader 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' (left not reported); the father's 'no arthritis' and 'no recurrent diarrhea' do not exclude the broader checklist items. Anal ulcer counted as 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' observed. Review-level percentages (89 patients from ref [4]) are not individual data. No internal contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: antipyretics (fever recurred); antibiotic treatment ineffective; tonsillectomy at 5 years of age (fever then recurred every 3 or 4 months); colchicine, with oral and genital ulcers disappearing after 9 months but fever continuing to recur; steroids and biologics under consideration
span: antipyretics decreased body temperature but high fever occurred again during episode
after tonsillectomy at 5 years of age, it recurred every 3 or 4 months
Colchicine was started, and 9 months after treatment, oral and genital ulcers disappeared. However, the fever continued to recur every 3 or 4 months.
Currently, we are considering treatments with immune suppressants such as steroids and biologics.
